svg.title: S3 — Connection / thread-pool exhaustion (traffic surge, slow downstream, N+1, lock queue)
svg.desc: Tests saturation-finder vs change-correlator disambiguation. The discriminating metric — pool WAIT time — was uninstrumented in almost every postmortem read (incident.io found a 20 s wait only by monkey-patching database/sql).
svg.text: S3 — Connection / thread-pool exhaustion (traffic surge, slow downstream, N+1, lock queue)

Tests saturation-finder vs change-correlator disambiguation. The discriminating metric — pool WAIT time — was uninstrumented in almost every postmortem read (incident.io found a 20 s wait only by monkey-patching database/sql).
pool in-use = max · pool wait appears
pgbouncer cl_waiting ↑ · FATAL too many conns
H1 lock queue · H2 slow query / bad plan
H3 many small holds · N+1 · needless txn
pool pending p99 18 s (E4) · DB CPU 30% (E5)
H1 ✗ (E1) · H2 ✗ (E2 fast) · H5 ✗ (E5 idle DB)
H4 open: pool cap unchanged? read config
wait high while DB idle? yes (E4+E5) → not DB
did span count rise at #390? yes (E3)
note: pool wait is the metric to alert on
6 raise pool caps — usually worsens; last
action: instrument pool wait; alert on it
runbook: no pool-cap raise before diagnosis

Discriminating queries: SQL pg_stat_activity by wait_event · blocked/blocking pg_locks join · pgbouncer SHOW POOLS (cl_waiting, maxwait) ‖ PromQL: hikaricp_connections_pending · go_sql_wait_duration_seconds_total · pgbouncer_pools_client_waiting_connections · idle-in-transaction count · per-trace DB span count.

Grounding (all READ): incident.io 2023 ‘database-performance’ — 2 weeks, 24 deploys, cause = needless transaction on Slack modal · incident.io 2023 ‘clouds, caches, connections’ — N+1 → anetd CPU · Slack 2020-05-12 HAProxy slots, scale-up ‘didn’t help at all’ · Slack 2022-02-22 Vitess scatter, metastable · Heroku lock-queue gist 25 min · GitLab 2023-10-30 48 min · CircleCI JVM pool shrink · incident.io PGAudit restart.

Why it matters to Smokejumper: the verifier must separate ‘DB is slow’ from ‘DB is idle but the app holds connections’ — E4+E5 together. Resolve and Cleric both centre ‘pool at 9x%’ as the clincher; the pool WAIT metric is sharper and rarer.
